idiom_name: Option::zip plus collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>() (fail-fast traverse); custom Validation for accumulation
implementation_notes: Rust has no higher-kinded types, so a generic Applicative trait cannot be written; the standard library supplies concrete pieces instead: Option::zip pairs independent optional values, and Iterator::collect into Result<Vec<_>, _> traverses a collection with fail-fast Result semantics. Result itself has no stable standard zip operation, so combine a fixed number of results with explicit matching or a crate. The question-mark operator and Result collection are therefore fail-fast tools; exhaustive validation needs an explicit error vector or a validation crate.
pitfalls: collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>() is fail-fast: it stops at the first Err and drops later failures, which is the opposite of what 'validate every field' callers usually expect.
Option::zip erases the reason for absence (two different failures become one None), so use Result when diagnostics matter.
partition yields Vec<Result<..>> halves: unwrapping the ok side afterwards reintroduces panics - convert with into_iter().flatten() or filter_map instead.
Collecting into Result<Vec<_>> allocates a Vec even when the result is an Err; for large inputs, short-circuit earlier with try_fold or a manual loop to avoid the wasted allocation.
